articles.title: Defining Radiographic Threshold Values for the Progressive Collapsing Foot Deformity Classification System: A Large-Cohort Diagnostic Study.
articles.authors: Belayneh R, Lintz F, Mansur NSB, Talaski G, Anderson D, Ellis SJ, et al.
articles.population: 154 healthy volunteers with neutral foot alignment or asymptomatic flatfoot, and 321 patients with progressive collapsing foot deformity
articles.outcomes: Established radiographic threshold values for classifying progressive collapsing foot deformity into 5 categories (A-E) based on computed tomography measurements
articles.take_home: Researchers identified specific measurement cut-off values on CT scans that can reliably help doctors classify different types of foot collapse, improving diagnostic accuracy and consistency in treatment planning. Most of these measurements had over 80% accuracy in distinguishing patients with foot collapse from those with normal feet.

articles.title: Predictors of Limited Weight-Bearing Dorsiflexion Following Total Ankle Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Thomas GM, McCahon JAS, Dulitzki Y, Chen Z, Parekh SG, Daniel JN, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent elective primary total ankle replacement between 2013 and 2023
articles.sample_size: 175 patients (111 with limited dorsiflexion, 64 with full dorsiflexion)
articles.outcomes: Postoperative dorsiflexion range of motion, functional scores (FAAM-ADL), pain scores (VAS), and patient satisfaction
articles.take_home: How much ankle movement you have before surgery is the best predictor of how much movement you will have after ankle replacement. Surgeons should discuss realistic expectations about post-operative ankle movement with patients beforehand to improve satisfaction.

articles.title: The Amount of Peroneus Longus Insertion Resection With Modified Lapidus Procedure for Severe Hallux Valgus: Comparative Radiographic Study of 2 Different Osteotomy Methods.
articles.authors: Sakurai S, Nakasa T, Ikuta Y, Ishibashi S, Moriwaki D, Chujo T, et al.
articles.outcomes: Amount of peroneus longus insertion resected with two different osteotomy methods; intermetatarsal angle correction; percentage of peroneus longus insertion resected
articles.take_home: When surgeons perform a modified Lapidus procedure for severe bunions by cutting the first metatarsal bone, they remove a large amount (over 50% on average) of an important muscle attachment that helps stabilise the foot. Cutting the bone at the cuneiform instead preserves more of this muscle attachment and may be better for long-term stability.

articles.title: Combined multi-ligament instability in patients with chronic symptoms following rotational ankle injuries. A prospective cohort study.
articles.authors: de Cesar Netto C, Casas EJH, Fayed A, Carvalho K, O'Neil C, Pozzessere E, et al.
articles.population: Adults with persistent pain and/or instability lasting more than 6 months after rotational ankle injuries who had not improved with non-surgical treatment
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes improved after surgery; 3 complications occurred (10% complication rate)
articles.take_home: Most patients with long-lasting ankle instability after rotational injuries have damage to multiple ligaments rather than just one, most commonly affecting three or more directions of stability. Surgery to repair all the damaged ligaments led to improvements in how patients felt and functioned, with a low risk of complications.

articles.title: Occult syndesmotic malreduction detected by postoperative CT despite acceptable radiographs: Association with 24-month functional outcomes.
articles.authors: Kassem E, Abolenain AS, Abdelazeem AH, Farag AW, El-Desouky M
articles.population: Adult patients undergoing ankle fracture fixation with syndesmotic stabilisation
articles.outcomes: CT-detected syndesmotic malreduction prevalence; AOFAS ankle-hindfoot scores at 24 months
articles.take_home: CT scans found that over half of patients had subtle misalignment of the syndesmosis that was not visible on standard X-rays, and this hidden misalignment was linked to worse ankle function at 2 years. Even minor degrees of malreduction were associated with poorer functional outcomes.

articles.title: Comparison of arthroscopic microfracture efficacy in osteochondral lesions of the talus with and without urate deposition.
articles.authors: Li Y, Hu L, Yang Y, An X, Liang Y, Xie X, et al.
articles.population: Patients with osteochondral lesions of the talus (ankle bone)
articles.outcomes: Pain (VAS score), ankle function (AOFAS score), cartilage healing (MOCART score), and complications at 24 months or longer follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients with urate crystal deposits in their ankle bone lesions had worse pain relief, poorer function, and slower cartilage healing after arthroscopic microfracture surgery compared to those without urate deposits. Having urate deposits and larger defects were identified as independent risk factors for poor outcomes.
